(2) Trusted-rules audit: PUT changing trusted_countries=[Canada,United States] + trusted_auditors=[alice@corp.com] wrote a db.audit_logs entry action='agent.trusted_rules_changed' with actor='jblan2026@gmail.com' and detail 'Trusted access rules changed — countries +[Canada, United States]; auditors +[alice@corp.com]'. Subsequent PUT with removed values wrote a second audit entry showing the removals in the detail diff. FRONTEND: Defensibility -> Governance settings shows gov-instant-alerts checkbox (unchecked at baseline); toggling it on + gov-save then hard reload restores checked=true (persisted). Sidebar red nav-watchtower-badge (28) appeared within ~3-5s of PUT trusted_countries=[US]. Clicking it navigated to /app/control-assurance?watch=1 with ca-globe-filter-suspicious AND ca-globe-range-24h both carrying the active 'bg-ai/15' class; globe rendered only the red Australia pin (Suspicious=28); page shows '24h' selector active in header range chips (All/24h/7d/30d/90d). Screenshot saved. FINAL RESET confirmed via GET: trusted_countries=[], trusted_ip_ranges=[], trusted_auditors=[], unusual_access_threshold=1, instant_suspicious_alerts=false; watchtower badge hidden after reset.
critical_code_review_comments: The trusted-rules audit diff in agents.py (~L2547-L2561) correctly separates label per resource ('countries', 'networks', 'auditors') and reports +[added] / -[removed] using sorted set diffs — precise and human-readable in the audit log. Wrapping the whole audit write in try/except keeps the PUT idempotent even if audit-log write ever fails, though this silences legitimate write errors. Consider logging (not raising) the exception for future observability.

_instant_suspicious_check (~L1796) short-circuits cleanly on: no org, alerts off, no trust configured, trusted_auditor whitelist, and trusted IP-range membership BEFORE running the more expensive geo_lookup. This ordering is exactly right for a hot fire-and-forget path.

The four call sites for _instant_suspicious_check use asyncio.create_task or bare fire pattern implicitly (via try/except pass) — public card/room open+download measured <2s end-to-end with alerts on, confirming they're non-blocking.
access-globe days whitelist expanded to (1, 7, 30, 90) cleanly — no arbitrary window abuse risk; any other value including negative/huge integers falls back to all-time.
The 'no audit when only instant toggled' behavior is enforced structurally (audit only when a diff exists on trusted_countries/ip_ranges/auditors) — good separation of concerns.
